messages.subject: time varying coefficient logistic model
parts:
Hi All:

I am working on a project which try to fit a time varying coefficient logistic model. Is there any way to implement this model into stan ? Or any reference about time varying coefficient Bayesian modeling will be appreciate. Thanks in advance.  The model I want to fit is 

y_i(t) | p_i(t) ~ Bernoulli( p_i(t) )
p_i(t) = beta(t) * x
beta(t) ~ Normal(0, 1/100) 

I am thinking there should be a smooth penalize for beta(t) but I did not know how to add it in my model.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] time varying coefficient logistic model
parts:
On 6/2/13 4:45 PM, Yilong wrote:
> Hi All:
>
> I am working on a project which try to fit a time varying coefficient logistic model. Is there any way to implement this
> model into stan ?

All you need to be able to do in Stan is write
down the log probability function.

Or any reference about time varying coefficient Bayesian modeling will be appreciate. Thanks in
> advance. The model I want to fit is
>
> y_i(t) | p_i(t) ~ Bernoulli( p_i(t) )
> p_i(t) = beta(t) * x
> beta(t) ~ Normal(0, 1/100)
>
> I am thinking there should be a smooth penalize for beta(t) but I did not know how to add it in my model.

Following your subject, I'd be inclined to put beta on the
logistic scale and model it as usual. In Stan, the model
would be:

model {
// priors
sigma ~ cauchy(0,5);
beta[1] ~ normal(0,1);
for (t in 2:T)
beta[t] ~ normal(beta[t-1],sigma);

// likelihood
for (n in 1:N)
for (t in 1:T)
y[n,t] ~ bernoulli(inv_logit(beta[t] * x[n,t]));
}

The likelihood is more efficiently and arithmetically stably
expressed using vectorization and the bernoulli_logit distribution
as:

for (n in 1:N)
y[n] ~ bernoulli_logit(beta * x[n]);

The logit parameterization of the Bernoulli is just defined
by

bernoull_logit(...) =def= bernoulli(inv_logit(...))

- Bob
